content.value_statement: Blockchain bots need careful event handling and operational safeguards. This skill guides Silverback bot design, implementation, testing, and deployment with risk controls.
actual_capabilities: Directs the assistant to fetch current Silverback documentation before writing code.
Helps choose triggers such as new blocks, event logs, cron jobs, and metrics.
Outlines a simple bot project structure with README, pyproject, and bot files.
Encourages staged testing before adding signers or critical communication channels.
Suggests limits, circuit breakers, and operational modes for safer bot behavior.
Shows user-visible commands for installing and running the Silverback CLI.
limitations: It depends on current Silverback documentation, so the assistant must fetch references before coding.
It assumes uv, Python, Ape, and Silverback are appropriate for the user environment.
It provides guidance and examples, not a complete production bot by itself.
Bots that sign transactions or post messages require careful user review and monitoring.

use_cases.title: Build Contract Event Bots
use_cases.description: Create a Silverback bot that listens for smart contract events and responds with controlled actions.

use_cases.title: Monitor Protocol Operations
use_cases.description: Track on-chain metrics and define safe thresholds before automated actions are enabled.

use_cases.title: Prepare Runtime Runbooks
use_cases.description: Document dependencies, run commands, logs, shutdown behavior, and staged testing for bot operations.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Starter Bot
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to plan a Silverback bot for [network]. It should monitor [event] and describe required docs, triggers, files, and tests.

prompt_templates.title: Draft Event Handling
prompt_templates.prompt: Use current Silverback docs to draft a bot that reacts to [contract event]. Include safe logging, configuration needs, and review points.

prompt_templates.title: Add Safety Controls
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this bot idea and add limits, circuit breakers, staged modes, and monitoring steps before any signer is enabled.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Deployment Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a deployment review for a Silverback bot on [ecosystem:network]. Cover dependencies, run commands, failure handling, and rollback steps.

output_examples.input: Monitor a token transfer event and alert a team channel.
output_examples.output: A bot plan with documentation links to fetch, contract configuration, event trigger design, alert flow, logging, and manual approval steps.

output_examples.input: Create a bot that reacts when trading volume crosses a threshold.
output_examples.output: A metric-driven design with threshold settings, dry-run behavior, circuit breaker conditions, and a staged path toward production use.

output_examples.input: Prepare a runbook for testing a Silverback bot on a target network.
output_examples.output: A concise checklist for dependencies, environment variables, run command review, log monitoring, shutdown behavior, and post-test questions.

best_practices: Fetch current Silverback documentation before generating implementation details.
Test with logging and non-signing modes before enabling transactions or external messages.
Use explicit limits, circuit breakers, and monitoring for every automated action.
anti_patterns: Do not enable a signer before the bot behavior is reviewed and tested.
Do not rely only on memory when current Silverback documentation is required.
Do not let a bot post messages or send transactions without operational safeguards.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps design and write Silverback bots that monitor blockchain events and trigger controlled actions.

faq.question: Does it fetch documentation automatically?
faq.answer: It instructs the assistant to fetch current Silverback documentation before writing code.

faq.question: Can it create production-ready bots?
faq.answer: It can guide production preparation, but users must review security, transactions, credentials, and operations.

faq.question: Which tools does it support?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What dependencies are expected?
faq.answer: The skill assumes uv can install the Silverback CLI and that Python dependencies can be configured.

faq.question: How should risky actions be handled?
faq.answer: Use staged testing, logs, configurable limits, circuit breakers, and explicit user approval before enabling signers.
